subject: Path to production: evaluation and handoff
messages:
From: Adrian Cole <adrian.cole@curewellhealth.com>
To: vivek_kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Path to production: evaluation and handoff

Hi Vivek / Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo on Wednesday — the model throughput and the token-cost breakdown were helpful. Our leadership wants a short, concrete plan we can use to run a 6-week technical evaluation and decide whether to move to production. Specifically they want:

- A mutual action plan (MAP) that lists milestones, owners, and signoff criteria.
- Clear exit gates for the evaluation (what constitutes pass/fail).
- A short set of acceptance tests we can run against our sample workload (functional & non-functional).
- Any procurement/legal deliverables (SLA, data residency, contract timeline) that would block go/no-go.

Can you send a draft MAP and acceptance test cases by next week? We are aiming to have procurement ready to sign off by 12/10 if the tech evaluation looks good.

Also copying procurement and our external consultant Elaine for any compliance questions.

Cheers,
Adrian
CTO, CureWell Health
From: vivek_kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
To: Adrian Cole <adrian.cole@curewellhealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Path to production: evaluation and handoff — draft MAP attached

Adrian —

Appreciate the clarity. Attached is a first-pass MAP and a short CSV of prompts/samples for your team to use in acceptance testing (RW-CureWell_MAP_v1.xlsx; CureWell_sample_prompts.csv). High-level proposal below — please flag anything missing.

Overview (6-week technical evaluation)
- Week 0 (align): sign MAP, provide sample data and API access to a dedicated pilot namespace. Owner: CureWell / Redwood (mutual).
- Weeks 1–2 (integration): SDK integration, initial latency/throughput smoke tests, and baseline functional checks. Owner: CureWell engineering; Redwood support on-call.
- Weeks 3–4 (stress + quality): run representative load (concurrent users), run acceptance test suite against sample prompts, collect quality metrics. Owner: CureWell engineering; Redwood infra lead.
- Week 5 (security & policy checks): provide SOC2 evidence, data retention config, and run data-residency verification on private pilot if required. Owner: Redwood security + CureWell compliance.
- Week 6 (signoff): present metrics and decision; execute procurement if pass.

Proposed exit gates (examples)
- Functional: API integration completed and authenticated; end-to-end flows (5 core user journeys) return correct structured output for >= 85% of sampled cases.
- Latency: p95 generation latency <= 300ms for payloads up to 512 tokens under expected concurrency.
- Throughput: system sustains target concurrency with <5% error rate for 30-minute sustained window.
- Quality: ranked results reach MRR >= 0.7 on the provided test corpus; hallucination/critical failures < 2%.
- Security/compliance: evidence for SOC2 in-scope controls shared; data retention policy applied to pilot namespace.

Acceptance tests (executable, short list)
1) Integration smoke: authentication, endpoint reachability, KV cache warming. (owner: CureWell)
2) Functional correctness: run 100 labelled prompts; must meet labels for intent & entities on >=85%. (owner: CureWell + Redwood)
3) Regression quality: run previous production prompts (if available) against model variant; delta in MRR <= -0.05. (owner: Redwood)
4) Performance under load: synthetic load test to target concurrency for 30 minutes; measure p95/p99 and error rates. (owner: CureWell infra, Redwood infra helps run test harness)
5) Data residency check: if private region requested, confirm logs and data remain in requested region. (owner: Redwood Security)

Next steps: please review the attachment and we will incorporate your procurement constraints. If this looks conceptually correct I can circulate a cleaned MAP with dates and owners by Tue 11/24.

-Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Thanks Vivek / Marissa — this looks good. A couple of asks to add into the MAP before we sign:

1) Data residency test: we must prove that no logs leave our EU region for any EU-subject data. If you can provide a runbook and a verification test that would close this gap.
2) End-user latency under load: our product team needs the 95th percentile under realistic UI load (simulated 120 concurrent sessions) to be <250ms for the top-critical flows.

If you can add those two gating checks and a short owner table we can sign by 12/03 and have procurement complete the legal review by 12/10.

-Adrian
CTO, CureWell Health

Adding measurement notes + owners for the MAP:

- Integration smoke (owner: CureWell eng; Redwood SE supports): verification checklist in pilot-measurement-spec.md.
- Functional correctness (owner: CureWell QA; Redwood provides labelled evaluation harness). Pass threshold: 85% intent/entity match.
- Quality/regression (owner: Redwood research; metric owner: Redwood + CureWell agreed signal). We will supply baseline MRR and run relative comparison.

Team —

Thanks all for the quick turns. I consolidated changes and attached the final MAP (RW-CureWell_MAP_v1.xlsx) and the measurement spec (pilot-measurement-spec.md). Below is the finalized signoff checklist and owners; please review and confirm by EOD 12/03 if this matches your expectations.

Final signoff checklist (key exit gates)
- MAP signed by both parties (deadline: 2026-12-03) — owner: Adrian / Marissa
- Integration complete: SDK + auth + E2E smoke (deadline: 2026-12-10) — owner: CureWell eng / Redwood SE
- Functional acceptance: 85%+ on labelled sample (deadline: 2026-12-17) — owner: CureWell QA / Redwood research
- Performance: p95 <= 250ms under 120 concurrent sessions for critical flows (deadline: 2026-12-17) — owner: Redwood infra + CureWell infra
- Regression quality: delta MRR >= -0.05 vs baseline (deadline: 2026-12-17) — owner: Redwood research
- Security/compliance: data residency test passed, SOC2 evidence shared (deadline: 2026-12-10) — owner: Redwood Security + CureWell compliance

Action items (owners)
- Vivek: circulate signed MAP template and finalize pilot access (due 12/03).
- Marissa: finalize pilot commercial terms and issue LOI template for procurement (due 12/03).
- Ben: share evaluation harness and runbook link (done).
- Adrian: provide sample labelled dataset and confirm concurrency profile (due 12/05).

If everyone confirms, we will treat 12/17 as the hard evaluation completion date and schedule a close review the week of 12/20. If pass, production rollout planning will start immediately with procurement completion targeted 12/31.

Thanks — I look forward to the signoff.

-Vivek
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
